ui.eyebrow: A small plan for your family
ui.title: Pause first. Call someone you know.
ui.intro: An urgent message can sound convincing. Agree on a family phrase, keep a reminder card, and practise spotting requests that need a second check.
ui.phraseTitle: A phrase you agree on together
ui.phraseIntro: Choose a phrase privately with your family. Do not use a password you already use elsewhere. You can leave this field empty.
ui.phrasePrivacy: Only in this open page. Never sent or saved. Reloading clears it. Maximum 80 characters, including joined emoji as one character.
ui.phraseTooLong: Please use no more than 80 characters. Your phrase has not been shortened.
ui.phraseUnsupported: This browser cannot safely check the phrase length. Leave the phrase empty to print the reminder card.
ui.includePhrase: Include my phrase on the printed card
ui.cardTitle: Urgent request? Pause. Hang up. Call back.
ui.cardPause: Do not send money, share a login code, or follow a link while someone is rushing you.
ui.cardCall: Call the person using a number you already know. Do not use a number or link from the urgent message.
ui.cardAsk: If you cannot reach them, check with another trusted person, even if the message asks you to keep it secret.
ui.phraseLimit: A familiar voice or a correct phrase alone is not proof of identity. Still call back on a known number.
ui.practiceIntro: These ten messages are fictional. Eight need a pause and a separate check; two are ordinary requests. Choose, read the explanation, then move on.
ui.resultAdvice: You can practise again. In a real situation, take your time and check using a number you already know. A score cannot verify a person or promise protection.
ui.shareTitle: Send the page, not your phrase
ui.sharePrivacy: These links share only this app. Agree on your private phrase separately with your family.
ui.shareText: A family reminder: pause and call back on a known number. Try ten fictional messages here.
ui.metricsPrivacy: Practice sends only an anonymous attempt ID, version, starting language, correct/incorrect answers and completion. No phrase, message text or contact details. Attempts are retained for eight UTC days.
ui.fictionNote: Learning material, not identity verification. No account needed.

1.message: It's your cousin. I'm in trouble and need you to transfer money right now. Please don't call me.
1.explanation: Urgency and pressure not to call deserve a pause. Call your cousin on a number you already know before sending anything.

2.message: Hi Mum, my phone broke. This is my new number. Can you pay a bill for me today?
2.explanation: A new number and a payment request need a separate check. Contact your family member using their known number or another trusted channel.

3.message: Your brother asked me to collect emergency money. Keep this between us so the rest of the family doesn't worry.
3.explanation: Secrecy can stop you from checking a story. Pause and speak with your brother or another trusted family member using a known contact.

4.message: I'm stranded. Buy gift cards and send me photos of the codes so I can get home.
4.explanation: Gift-card codes can be spent as soon as they are shared. Do not send them. Verify the request by calling a number you know.

5.message: This is your bank's security team. Move your savings to our safe account now while we fix the problem.
5.explanation: A request to move money to a supposed safe account needs a pause. End the conversation and contact your bank using its official number.

6.message: Your account will close today. Open the sign-in link in this message and enter your password to keep it.
6.explanation: Do not follow an unexpected sign-in link. Open the service independently through its known app or address and check there.

7.message: I'm helping you fix your account. Tell me the one-time login code that just arrived on your phone.
7.explanation: A login code can give someone access to your account. Do not share it with the sender. Contact the service independently if you need help.

8.message: I work for a senior official. Please send a copy of your identity document through this chat immediately.
8.explanation: A claimed title does not verify a sender. Pause and check the request through an independently known official channel before sharing documents.

9.message: Shall we have our usual family dinner at six or seven on Sunday?
9.explanation: This example only asks about a dinner time, with no link, payment or private information. It is an ordinary request; that still does not prove who sent it.

10.message: When you have time, could you send me the soup recipe we talked about? No rush.
10.explanation: This example asks for a recipe without urgency, links or sensitive details. It is an ordinary request, not a guarantee of the sender's identity.
